guide.intro: RAR (Roshal Archive) is the proprietary archive format created by WinRAR, still the most common way large downloads, game mods, subtitles and document bundles are shared. Windows, iPhone and Chromebook can’t always open it out of the box, and many “free” unzip sites make you upload your files to a server. {brand} opens it right inside your browser tab – the files are listed with sizes, and you can save any one of them or everything as a single ZIP.
uses: Open a RAR you received by email or downloaded, on a computer where you can’t install software.
Pull a single document out of a large backup without unpacking everything.
Unpack archives on a Chromebook, iPad or phone.
Convert the contents into a regular ZIP that every device opens.
tips: Download everything as ZIP to repack the content in the most compatible format.
Only open archives from sources you trust – extracting is safe, but running unknown programs inside them is not.
For multi-part archives, join the parts on a desktop with 7-Zip first.
Need to make an archive? Use Create TAR.GZ or Create ZIP.
more: What is inside a RAR

An archive stores many files and folders as one, usually compressed. {brand} reads the directory, decompresses each entry in a background worker so the page stays responsive, and shows a list with full paths. Nothing runs from inside the archive – files are only offered as downloads.
Under the hood

Extraction uses libarchive – the same open-source BSD-licensed library behind the tar command on macOS and FreeBSD – compiled to WebAssembly (about 1 MB, loaded only when you press Start so the page itself stays instant).
Compared with other options

Desktop tools like 7-Zip and WinRAR are excellent but need installing (and WinRAR nags for a licence). Upload sites such as ezyZip or extract.me either upload your file or show ads and limits. Here nothing is uploaded, there are no limits and no sign-up.

faq.a: Empty folders are not listed and macOS metadata (__MACOSX, ._ files) is kept as-is. If an entry fails to decompress the archive may be damaged or a split volume.
Click any file in the list to download it; images and PDFs open directly in your browser.

guide.intro: TAR.GZ is the archive format servers, Linux distributions and developer tools expect. {brand} builds one in your browser – handy on Windows, ChromeOS and phones where you can’t run the tar command – without uploading a byte.
uses: Package website files or a project for upload to a Linux server.
Send logs or a folder of files as a single attachment.
Create backups in an open, long-lived format.
Prepare .7z archives for maximum compression.
tips: Already-compressed files (JPG, MP4, ZIP) barely shrink – choose plain .tar for them to save time.
Use .tar.xz for text-heavy folders such as logs or source code.
Name the archive with a date for easy backups.
more: TAR vs ZIP

ZIP compresses each file separately and is built into every OS. TAR bundles everything first and then compresses the whole stream, which usually yields smaller archives for many small files and keeps Unix permissions and long paths.
How it works

Your files are passed to libarchive (BSD licence) running as WebAssembly in a background worker. The compressed archive is written in memory and offered as a download. The 1 MB engine is loaded only when you press Start.

faq.a: Yes – use Extract TAR.GZ, Extract RAR or Extract 7Z.
